# Wymber

> Wymber is a privacy-first, local-first tool for mapping and understanding difficult
> experiences (trauma mapping). Your map lives in a single encrypted vault on your own
> device; there are no accounts and no servers holding user data. Free and open-source
> (AGPL-3.0). Currently in alpha at https://web.wymber.app. Wymber is a self-help tool
> for personal reflection, not therapy, diagnosis, or a crisis service.

Citation is welcome; we decline AI training (see /robots.txt Content Signals).

## Pages

- [Home](https://wymber.app/): what Wymber is, how it works, the privacy promise, and a FAQ (trauma mapping, where data lives, therapy, cost, AI, forgotten passwords, offline use, encrypted journals)
- [Privacy](https://wymber.app/privacy): the plain-language privacy policy
- [About](https://wymber.app/about): who makes Wymber and why
- [Sources](https://wymber.app/sources): the trauma-informed research behind the design
- [What's new](https://wymber.app/changelog): the human changelog

## Learn

- [What is trauma mapping?](https://wymber.app/trauma-mapping): the practice and its lineage (trauma egg, trauma timeline)
- [How to make a trauma timeline](https://wymber.app/trauma-timeline): a gentle step-by-step guide to mapping events chronologically, with a safety note and reflection prompts
- [Is there a trauma egg app?](https://wymber.app/trauma-egg-app): no official one exists; Wymber as an independent, private, digital tool in that spirit (not the Murray Method, not affiliated)
- [How to do the trauma egg exercise](https://wymber.app/trauma-egg-exercise): a gentle paper-first step-by-step with a worked example (educational, independent of Marilyn Murray's Murray Method, not therapy)
- [How Wymber encrypts your map](https://wymber.app/encryption): AES-256-GCM on-device, envelope encryption, verifiable in the open code
- [What happens if you forget your password?](https://wymber.app/recovery): the recovery code as a second key of equal power, why there's no rotation today, and why losing both is permanent
- [Local-first](https://wymber.app/local-first): why mental-health data shouldn't live on someone's server
- [Trauma-informed design, applied](https://wymber.app/trauma-informed-design): SAMHSA's six principles as concrete software decisions
- [Backing up or syncing your map](https://wymber.app/cloud-sync): using a cloud service to back up or move the encrypted vault, manually, with the risks (no live sync yet)

## Code

- [GitHub](https://github.com/Tamok/wymber): the open-source client, so the privacy claims are auditable
